messages:
alex: CI red on `//runtime:once_backoff_test` on main — flaky assertion in backoff counter, failing ~1/30. Logs attached. Repro locally sometimes fails with `RuntimeError: expected 1 retries, got 0`
ci-bot: [build #12874] test failed: //runtime:once_backoff_test (see https://ci.redwood/internal/12874)
maria: @alex can you paste the failing stack? is this the recent retry refactor?
alex: stack trace snippet:
```
AssertionError: expected backoff triggers to be 1, got 0
  at tests/once_backoff_test.py:42
  at runtime/retry.py:88
```
sujay: fwiw i saw something like this earlier; could be timer coalescing + prefetched kv cache changing scheduling. try repeated runs with a seed or disable coalescing to rule that out.
jon: can we kick a bisect job with seed sweep and force single-thread runs? i'll start one on CI.
alex: ping @sujay for bisect? locally `pytest tests/once_backoff_test.py -k once_backoff -s --runslow` sometimes repros if I set `REPRO_SEED=238`.
sujay: i'll run a 100-seed sweep on CI with `--jobs=1` to avoid parallel noise, should be ~15m.
maria: also try env `RT_LOWER_JITTER=0` — if failure disappears it's likely jitter/timer alignment.
ci-bot: Bisect job queued: https://ci.redwood/internal/bisect/697 (claimed by sujay)
jon: quick note: temporary sleep(5ms) before first retry stabilizes it in my local runs but that's a bandaid. prefer root cause.
alex: filed issue INF-3124 with logs and repro steps: https://redwood/issues/INF-3124 — adding logs from build.
sujay: update: bisect found seed=238 reproduces on linux-x86 in CI; also saw seed=887 locally. I'll open a draft PR with extra instrumentation to capture schedule timing.
maria: if confirmed, let's add a deterministic variant of the test (disable jitter) and mark the flaky one with `@flaky` until fixed.
alex: sounds good. i'll add the flaky label and follow sujay's PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
sujay: adding notes to the bisect run, will comment back with exact timing diffs when available.
